title: Singular form review
focus: Apply learned KPT patterns in controlled genitive and minä forms.

exercises.instruction: Identify the consonant change in the supplied forms.
exercises.prompt: pankki (“bank”) → pankin (“of the bank”): which consonant change is shown?
exercises.explanation: Compare pankki with pankin. The double kk becomes a single k; the separate -n ending marks the genitive.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT recognition: form not yet correct

optionFeedback.k → ∅: One k remains in pankin. Here double kk becomes single k; a single k is not disappearing.
optionFeedback.kk → k: Correct. Pankki has kk and pankin has k.
optionFeedback.nk → ng: Pankin still has nk, not ng. The change is kk to k.

exercises.instruction: Identify the consonant change in the supplied forms.
exercises.prompt: leipä (“bread”) → leivän (“of the bread”): which consonant change is shown?
exercises.explanation: Compare leipä with leivän. The single p becomes v; the separate -n ending marks the genitive.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: KPT recognition: form not yet correct

optionFeedback.p → v: Correct. The p in leipä corresponds to v in leivän.
optionFeedback.pp → p: Leipä has one p, not pp. Here the single p becomes v.
optionFeedback.t → d: There is no t or d in this pair. Compare the p in leipä with v in leivän.

exercises.prompt: matto (“carpet”) → ____ (“of the carpet”)
exercises.explanation: Use the genitive ending -n and the weak stem mato-: tt becomes t, then mato- + n = maton (“of the carpet”).
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Genitive -n: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The genitive ending -n is right. Weaken tt to t before adding it: maton.
Matot means “carpets”. “Of the carpet” needs genitive -n: maton.

exercises.prompt: of the flower — use the supplied base kukka (“flower”)
exercises.explanation: kukka means “flower”; kukan means “the flower's / of the flower”. The genitive ends in -n. kk weakens to k.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Genitive -n: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Use the weak stem kuka- and the genitive ending -n: kukan.

exercises.prompt: hatun — from hattu (“hat”)
exercises.explanation: Hatun is the genitive of hattu (“hat”). It means “of the hat” or “the hat's”: tt becomes t and the ending is -n. Finnish has no word corresponding to the English article here.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Genitive -n: form not yet correct

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The ending is -n, which marks genitive here, not plural -t. Hatun means “of the hat”.
